CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old male presenting with a one-week history of cough productive of yellow sputum. Patient reports symptoms worsened over the past two days. He reports subjective feeling of warmth but denies taking temperature and denies fever. Denies shortness of breath. Reports congestion with post-nasal drainage and bilateral sinus pressure. Denies other household members being ill. Patient has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil with minimal symptom relief. Additionally, patient fell down approximately 4-5 stairs this morning while coughing, sustaining a right knee injury with pain on the medial aspect of the knee. Patient reports ability to ambulate with mild limp and denies sensation of instability. Has not taken any pain medication for the knee injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever (subjectively feels warm but did not measure temperature). Denies chills. Reports mild aches. Denies shortness of breath. Positive for nasal congestion, post-nasal drainage, and bilateral sinus pressure. Positive for right knee pain from trauma. All other systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
3. Dayquil (over-the-counter) for cough and cold symptoms

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. Married. Does not monitor blood pressure or blood glucose at home. Cleveland Browns football fan.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs:
- Temperature: 98.4°F (afebrile)
- Blood Pressure: 125/62 mmHg
- Heart Rate: 80s, regular
- Oxygen Saturation: 97% on room air

HEENT:
- Facial exam: Bilateral pain to palpation of maxillary sinuses
- Nasal exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge
- Throat exam: Midline uvula; no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space

Neck: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy

Lungs: Coarse rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough

Heart: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmur appreciated

Right Knee: Pain to palpation, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis of medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Pending studies ordered:
- Right knee X-ray
- Chest X-ray (if symptoms worsen)
- Lipid panel
- Hemoglobin A1c

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cough/Upper Respiratory Infection with Mild Bronchitis
   Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis. Continue supportive care and over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg orally twice daily for expectoration. No antibiotics indicated at this time. Patient instructed to contact office if symptoms worsen; chest X-ray to be obtained if needed to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right Knee Pain - Right Medial Collateral Ligament Strain
   Right medial collateral ligament strain from fall this morning. Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg orally once daily. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening. Right knee X-ray ordered to rule out osseous injury.

3. Hypertension
   Hypertension currently well-controlled on current therapy. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel to assess cardiovascular risk. Counseled on importance of blood pressure monitoring and dietary salt restriction.

4. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
   Type 2 diabetes on metformin therapy. Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed. Counseled on importance of blood glucose monitoring and dietary sugar intake. Patient instructed to report blood glucose readings via patient portal.
